data.content:
companionship,parentage	Hermes
Zeus
Zeus was Hermes's father, and Zeus and Hermes travelled together disguised as ordinary men.

devotion,marriage	Baucis
Philemon
Baucis and Philemon were a devoted married couple whom Zeus agreed never to separate.

exception,survival	Baucis and Philemon's Hut
Zeus's Flood
Baucis and Philemon's hut was the only home in the valley not destroyed by Zeus's flood.

causation,punishment	Zeus
Zeus's Flood
Zeus caused the flood to punish people who refused Zeus and Hermes food and shelter.

hospitality	Philemon
Zeus
Philemon offered Zeus food, wine, and overnight shelter.

hospitality	Baucis
Zeus
Baucis offered Zeus food, wine, and overnight shelter.

hospitality	Hermes
Philemon
Philemon offered Hermes food, wine, and overnight shelter.

reward,transformation	Baucis and Philemon's Hut
Zeus
Zeus transformed Baucis and Philemon's hut into a temple to reward the couple's kindness.

religious service,residence	Philemon
Temple
Philemon lived in the temple as a priest.

hospitality	Baucis
Hermes
Baucis offered Hermes food, wine, and overnight shelter.

parentage	Athena
Zeus
Athena was Zeus's daughter.

transformation	Baucis and Philemon's Hut
Temple
Baucis and Philemon's hut became the temple where the couple spent the remainder of their lives.

transformation	Oak and Linden Trees
Philemon
Philemon and Baucis became oak and linden trees with entwined branches after death; the text does not assign a particular tree species to Philemon.

patronage contest,rejection	Athens
Poseidon
Poseidon sought to protect Athens, but the citizens preferred Athena's gift and chose Athena.

religious service,residence	Baucis
Temple
Baucis lived in the temple as a priestess.

rivalry	Athena
Poseidon
Athena and Poseidon competed to become the protector of the city later named Athens.

civic benefit,gift	Athens
Olive Tree
The citizens of Athens preferred the useful olive tree to Poseidon's gift.

transformation	Baucis
Oak and Linden Trees
Baucis and Philemon became oak and linden trees with entwined branches after death; the text does not assign a particular tree species to Baucis.

creation,gift	Poseidon
Poseidon's River
Poseidon created the river as a gift intended to impress the citizens.

invention,music	Hermes
Lyre
Hermes created the first lyre from a tortoise shell and strings and played music on the instrument.

gift,rejection	Athens
Poseidon's River
The citizens of Athens initially admired Poseidon's river but reconsidered after tasting the saltwater.

causation,retaliation	Poseidon
Poseidon's Flood
Poseidon caused a terrible flood after the citizens selected Athena as protector.

acquisition,theft	Apollo's Cattle
Hermes
Hermes stole and hid Apollo's cattle, then received permission to keep the cattle in exchange for the lyre.

namesake,protection	Athena
Athens
The citizens chose Athena as protector, named Athens after Athena, and became strong and prosperous with Athena's help.

exchange,ownership	Apollo
Apollo's Cattle
Apollo originally owned the cattle and later exchanged the cattle for Hermes's lyre.

equipment,mobility	Hermes
Winged Hat and Sandals
Hermes wore a winged hat and sandals that enabled rapid travel for delivering messages.

capital	Athens
Greece
Athens is the capital city of Greece.

creation,gift	Athena
Olive Tree
Athena caused an olive tree to grow by striking the ground with a spear and offered the tree to the citizens.

care,parentage	Ares
Zeus
Zeus was Ares's father and bandaged Ares's wound, although Zeus was not proud of Ares's conduct.

barter	Apollo's Cattle
Lyre
The lyre was exchanged for permission for Hermes to keep Apollo's cattle.

participation	Ares
Trojan War
Ares participated in the Trojan War and changed allegiance from a promised commitment to the Greeks to support for the Trojans.

exchange,possession	Apollo
Lyre
Apollo accepted the lyre in exchange for the cattle and subsequently carried the instrument.

disloyalty,promised support	Ares
Greeks
Ares promised to help the Greeks but did not honor the commitment.

exchange,reconciliation	Apollo
Hermes
Hermes enchanted Apollo with lyre music, leading Apollo to accept the instrument instead of recovering the stolen cattle.

participation	Trojan War
Trojans
The Trojans were a side in the Trojan War.

military support	Ares
Trojans
Ares helped the Trojans after Aphrodite's persuasion.

participation	Greeks
Trojan War
The Greeks were a side in the Trojan War.

creation,inscription,provocation	Eris
Golden Apple
Eris made the golden apple and inscribed the words “For the fairest.”<SEP>Eris made the golden apple and inscribed “For the fairest” to provoke competition among goddesses.

love,persuasion	Aphrodite
Ares
Ares was in love with Aphrodite, who persuaded Ares to support the Trojans.

identity	Diomedes
Greeks
Diomedes was identified as a Greek mortal.

competition,intended discovery	Golden Apple
Hera
Eris left the golden apple where Hera would find the apple.<SEP>Eris left the golden apple for Hera and two other goddesses; Hera believed Hera deserved the apple as the fairest.

ownership,residence	Baucis
Baucis and Philemon's Hut
Baucis owned and lived in the hut with Philemon.

advocacy	Aphrodite
Trojans
Aphrodite persuaded Ares to help the Trojans.

combat,injury	Ares
Diomedes
Ares challenged Diomedes, and Diomedes wounded Ares.

competition,intended discovery	Athena
Golden Apple
Eris left the golden apple where Athena would find the apple.<SEP>Athena claimed to be the fairest goddess and competed for the golden apple.

ownership,residence	Baucis and Philemon's Hut
Philemon
Philemon owned and lived in the hut with Baucis.

discovery,ownership	Baucis
Wine Jug
Baucis shared the couple's only jug of wine with the visitors and noticed that the jug had been refilled.

possession,use	Poseidon
Poseidon's Trident
Poseidon carried the trident and struck the ground with the trident to release water.

competition,intended discovery	Aphrodite
Golden Apple
Eris left the golden apple where Aphrodite would find the apple.<SEP>Aphrodite competed for the golden apple and won Paris's judgment.

resource provision	Olive Tree
Olive Wood
The olive tree provided wood suitable for building and heating.

hospitality,ownership	Philemon
Wine Jug
Philemon and Baucis offered the visitors the couple's only jug of wine.

creation instrument	Poseidon's River
Poseidon's Trident
The strike of Poseidon's trident released water that became Poseidon's river.

cooking,source	Olive Oil
Olives
The olives provided oil that could be used for cooking.

attachment,construction	Lyre Strings
Tortoise Shell
Hermes tied the lyre strings across the tortoise shell to create the first lyre.

judgment,promise	Aphrodite
Paris
Paris selected Aphrodite as the fairest goddess after Aphrodite offered Paris the love of the world's most beautiful woman.

evaluation	Athena
Poseidon's River
Athena urged the citizens to taste the river water, exposing the unpleasant saltwater taste.

food provision,growth	Olive Tree
Olives
Edible olives grew on the olive tree.

causation,declaration	King of Sparta
Trojan War
The angry king of Sparta sent soldiers to declare war on Troy after Helen's departure, resulting in the Trojan War.

elopement	Helen
Paris
Paris and Helen ran away together to Troy.

warfare	Trojan War
Troy
Troy was the target of the Trojan War, which lasted ten years.

rulership	King of Sparta
Sparta
Helen's husband ruled Sparta.

persuasion,promise	Athena
Paris
Athena offered to make Paris a courageous and successful soldier to influence Paris's judgment.

unintended causation	Aphrodite
Trojan War
Aphrodite unintentionally helped start the Trojan War through the events following Paris's judgment.

marriage	Helen
King of Sparta
Helen was married to the king of Sparta when Helen ran away with Paris.

confinement,rulership	Hades
Underworld
Hades ruled the Underworld and was responsible for keeping the dead there for all time.

persuasion,promise	Hera
Paris
Hera promised to make Paris very powerful to influence Paris's judgment.

attempted rescue,marriage	Orpheus
Orpheus's Wife
Orpheus attempted to recover a deceased wife but looked back during departure, preventing the wife's release.

destination	Helen
Troy
Helen fled to Troy with Paris.

permanent confinement	Orpheus's Wife
Underworld
Orpheus's wife had to stay in the Underworld forever after Orpheus violated Hades's condition.

conditional permission,singing	Hades
Orpheus
Orpheus's singing enchanted Hades into permitting the return of Orpheus's wife, provided Orpheus did not look at the wife while leaving.

siblings	Poseidon
Zeus
Zeus and Poseidon were brothers.

destination	Paris
Troy
Paris fled to Troy with Helen.

journey,return	Orpheus
Underworld
Orpheus entered the Underworld to retrieve a deceased wife and unusually returned from the Underworld.

transportation	Four Black Horses
Hades's Chariot
Four black horses drew Hades's chariot.

siblings	Hades
Zeus
Hades and Zeus were brothers.

parentage,release,revenge	Hephaestus
Hera
Hephaestus was Hera's son, trapped Hera in revenge for poor mothering, and later freed Hera.

siblings	Hades
Poseidon
Hades and Poseidon were brothers.

creation,revenge	Golden Throne
Hephaestus
Hephaestus created the golden throne as a revenge gift for Hera.

restraint	Hera
Unbreakable Chains
Unbreakable chains bound Hera after Hera sat on the golden throne.

ownership	Hades
Hades's Chariot
Hades owned a chariot drawn by four black horses.

intervention,intoxication	Dionysus
Hephaestus
The gods asked Dionysus to intoxicate Hephaestus so Hephaestus could be brought to free Hera.

entrapment,gift	Golden Throne
Hera
Hera received the golden throne and became trapped after sitting on the throne.

siblings,twins	Apollo
Artemis
Artemis was Apollo's twin sister.

arrival,rescue	Hephaestus
Mount Olympus
After drinking heavily, Hephaestus was led to Mount Olympus to free Hera.

trap mechanism	Golden Throne
Unbreakable Chains
The golden throne trapped Hera using unbreakable chains.

evasion,love,pursuit	Alpheus
Artemis
Alpheus fell in love with Artemis and pursued Artemis, but Artemis evaded recognition by covering her face in mud.

love,rejected marriage	Apollo
Hestia
Apollo wished to marry Hestia, but Hestia declared that Hestia would never marry.

marriage,reward	Aphrodite
Hephaestus
The gods gave Aphrodite to Hephaestus as a wife in return for freeing Hera.

disguise,followers	Artemis
Artemis's Nymphs
Artemis's female followers joined Artemis in covering their faces with mud.

love,rejected marriage	Hestia
Poseidon
Poseidon wished to marry Hestia, but Hestia declared that Hestia would never marry.

gift	Key to Olympus
Zeus
Zeus gave the key to Olympus to Hestia as a token of appreciation.

failed recognition	Alpheus
Artemis's Nymphs
Alpheus could not distinguish Artemis from Artemis's mud-covered nymphs and abandoned the search.

appointment,appreciation	Hestia
Zeus
Zeus rewarded Hestia's resolution of the marriage dispute by assigning care of the gods' necessities and making Hestia goddess of the home and family.

association	Key to Olympus
Mount Olympus
The key given to Hestia was identified as a key to Olympus.

dedication,worship	Demeter
Demeter's Oak Tree
The oak tree was dedicated to Demeter and used by local people as a place to make vows to Demeter.

receipt	Hestia
Key to Olympus
Hestia received a key to Olympus from Zeus.

location	Demeter's Oak Tree
Thessaly
Demeter's huge oak tree stood in Thessaly.

throne transfer	Dionysus
Hestia
Hestia willingly gave up a throne for Dionysus to preserve a quiet and peaceful life.

appearance,punishment,warning	Demeter
Erysichthon
Demeter appeared to Erysichthon in goddess form and punished Erysichthon with a curse.<SEP>Demeter appeared first as a priest to warn Erysichthon, then in goddess form to punish Erysichthon for continuing to cut the oak.

membership,seniority	Hestia
Mount Olympus
Hestia was the oldest of the gods of Olympus.

parentage	Dionysus
Zeus
Dionysus was described as Zeus's half-son.

destruction	Demeter's Oak Tree
Erysichthon
Erysichthon cut down Demeter's oak tree to make a banqueting table after the slaves refused.

imposition,punishment	Curse of Insatiable Hunger
Demeter
Demeter imposed the curse of insatiable hunger as punishment for Erysichthon.<SEP>Demeter imposed the curse of insatiable hunger as punishment for cutting down the dedicated oak.

arrival,throne demand	Dionysus
Mount Olympus
Dionysus went to Olympus demanding a throne.

command,enslavement	Erysichthon
Erysichthon's Slaves
Erysichthon ordered the slaves to cut down Demeter's oak tree.

refusal	Demeter's Oak Tree
Erysichthon's Slaves
Erysichthon's slaves refused to cut down the oak tree dedicated to Demeter.

affliction,perpetual hunger	Curse of Insatiable Hunger
Erysichthon
Erysichthon was afflicted with a curse that prevented Erysichthon's hunger from ever being satisfied.<SEP>The curse ensured that Erysichthon's hunger would never be satisfied.

dismissal	Demeter
Erysichthon's Slaves
Demeter sent Erysichthon's slaves away before punishing Erysichthon.

dismissal	Demeter
Slaves
Demeter sent away the slaves before punishing Erysichthon.
